content: Interest speaks all sorts of tongues, and plays all sorts of characters; even that of disinterestedness.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Water is the softest thing on earth, yet it carves through solid granite. It doesn't fight obstacles; it yields, flows around them, and quietly finds its way to its natural level.

In François de La Rochefoucauld's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. When we force outcomes with brute willpower and anxiety, we exhaust ourselves and create unnecessary resistance. Aligning with nature means trusting the timing of things and moving with steady, patient persistence.
reflectionPrompt: What hidden motive, insecurity, or fear might be silently driving your recent reactions?
